subject: Technical walkthrough for CloudSpark — scheduling a short engineer-led demo
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: John Park <john@cloudspark.io>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Technical walkthrough for CloudSpark — scheduling a short engineer-led demo

Hi John —

Thanks for trying our Quickstart docs and spinning up the sample on your side. The docs CTA routed your sign-up to me — I work with developer accounts and can set up a short technical walkthrough with one of our engineers to cover:

- a quick review of how you ran the Quickstart
- recommended model/quantization profiles for low-latency inference
- deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC) and what we recommend for audit/data controls

Are you available for a 30-minute slot this week? A few windows in PST that work for us:
- Tue 12/08 10:00–10:30 PST
- Tue 12/08 14:00–14:30 PST
- Wed 12/09 09:00–09:30 PST

If none of those fit, reply with preferred days/times and your timezone and I’ll adapt. I’ve attached a very short pre-demo checklist so our engineer can tailor the walkthrough.

Also CC’ing Vivek (infrastructure/serving lead) who will join the call for deeper runtime questions.

Cheers,
Camila Reyes | Account Executive, Developer GTM
Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

Attachment: redwood_quickstart-checklist.pdf (2 pages)
From: John Park <john@cloudspark.io>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Technical walkthrough for CloudSpark — scheduling a short engineer-led demo

Thanks Camila — appreciate the quick follow-up.

We’re on Eastern (EST). Prefer afternoons EST. This week I can do:
- Wed 12/09 13:00–13:30 EST (which I think is 10:00–10:30 PST)
- Thu 12/10 15:00–15:30 EST

A couple of notes up front: we’re evaluating Redwood for a low-latency search/assistant feature. Our infra is currently on AWS (us-east-1) and we’re interested in private deployment options and SOC 2 evidence; I saw references in the docs but would like to cover the specifics.

Also: is it okay to record the session for product team review?

—John
John Park | Senior DevRel, CloudSpark
john@cloudspark.io
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: John Park <john@cloudspark.io>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Technical walkthrough for CloudSpark — scheduling a short engineer-led demo

Perfect — thanks for the timezone. Wed 12/09 13:00 EST (10:00 PST) works for both me and Vivek.

I’ve created a quick scheduling link if you need to pick a different slot: https://calendly.com/redwood/technical-walkthrough-30m — but I’ll tentatively hold Wed 12/09 10:00–10:30 PST and send the calendar invite once you confirm.

Quick logistics:
- We can record the session; we’ll only retain recording for internal review unless you ask otherwise. If you need a formal NDA or SOC 2 artifacts shared before the call we can route that via our security team.
- Please attach or paste one sample prompt or a short description of the inference pattern (few-shot, chat-like, ranking) — Vivek will use that to prepare tailored examples.

Attaching the Quickstart checklist again and a tiny text note where you can paste the sample prompt.

Thanks —
Camila

Attachment: redwood_quickstart-checklist.pdf
Attachment: cloudspark-prod-topology.txt (placeholder for environment notes)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: John Park <john@cloudspark.io>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Technical walkthrough for CloudSpark — scheduling a short engineer-led demo

Hi John — quick intro, I’ll be the engineer on the call. A couple of quick asks so we make the 30 minutes productive:

- If you can paste a short example prompt or a 3–5 line example input that represents your common traffic, that helps a lot.
- Let me know expected QPS and typical sequence length (tokens) — ballpark numbers are fine.
- If you’re using a particular open model family (e.g., Llama 2, Mistral, Llama 3), tell us which so we can prep quantization/latency pointers.

I’ll prepare a short demo showing: a) serving profile for low-latency, b) a quick cost estimate for hosted vs. dedicated for your volume, c) what the VPC/private control plane looks like and typical audit logs available.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime
Vivek@redwood.com
From: John Park <john@cloudspark.io>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 18:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Technical walkthrough for CloudSpark — scheduling a short engineer-led demo

Sounds good — Wed 12/09 13:00 EST confirmed.

Sample prompt below (feel free to adapt):

"User: Find me API endpoints that match "S3 signed URL" error patterns and show remediation steps.
Assistant: Provide ranked responses and a short code snippet for patching."

Expected traffic: small PoC for now — ~5 QPS peak, median sequence length ~120 tokens. We’re experimenting with Llama 2-Chat family.

Recording is fine. Please send a calendar invite and attach any pre-read.

—John
